title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Organizational messages can be delivered by email
summary: The authoring controls, approval behavior and roadmap details are supported. Microsoft sources disagree about the number of email templates; the briefing should acknowledge that discrepancy.

claims.claim: Writer assignments are available in the Microsoft 365 admin center through Show all > Users > Active users > user > Roles > Manage roles > Admin center access > Show all by category > Other > Organizational Messages Writer.
claims.quote: In the user's details pane, select Manage roles under Roles. In the Manage admin roles pane, select Admin center access, and then select Show all by category. Scroll down to the Other section.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns an Entra role, with roleDefinitionId selecting the Writer or Approver role.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
    {
        "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.unifiedRoleAssignment",
        "principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>",
        "roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>",
        "directoryScopeId": "/"
    }

claims.claim: The email location is selected through Show all > Reports > Organizational messages > Top actions > Create a message > Objective > Location in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Under the Top actions section of the Organizational messages page, select Create a message.

claims.claim: No API or cmdlet for creating an organizational message and selecting email delivery is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "API" "create" "cancel"; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "organizational messages" "create"; "organizational messages" "PowerShell" "schedule" "cancel". Opened the cited organizational messages guide and FAQ; no authoring API reference found.

claims.claim: Recipient groups are configured through Show all > Reports > Organizational messages > Top actions > Create a message > Objective > Location > Template > Customize > Recipients.
claims.quote: Recipients: Set the groups within your organization that should receive the message.

claims.claim: No API for setting organizational-message recipient targeting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "Graph" "schedule" "recipients" "API"; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "organizational messages" "create". Opened the organizational messages guide and FAQ; results document recipient selection in the UI, not an organizational-message targeting API.

claims.claim: Show all > Reports > Organizational messages > Manage messages is the documented location for cancelling or deleting messages.
claims.quote: From Manage messages, your team can perform the following actions on messages: / Cancel, delete, approve, and copy messages.

claims.claim: No API or cmdlet for cancelling or deleting organizational messages is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "API" "create" "cancel"; "organizational messages" "PowerShell" "schedule" "cancel". Opened the cited organizational messages guide and FAQ; search results expose UI cancellation and unrelated calendar commands, not a message cancellation API.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Email delivery is admin-opt-in: an authorized author creates and schedules a message rather than emails being sent merely because the channel is available.
claims.quote: If you have the Organizational Messages Writer Microsoft Entra role, you can create a new organizational message. / Finish: Review the message before scheduling or sending for approval by your organization's approvers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model for pre-made email messages is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages Microsoft 365 email templates licensing schedule; "organizational messages" "email" "license" "price". Opened the feature guide's Requirements and advanced-features licensing and the FAQ's license section; neither states an email entitlement.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Organizational messages now support email alongside existing Windows and Teams delivery surfaces.
claims.quote: Email Messages: Admins can now deliver premade templatized messages by email, joining existing surfaces like Windows Spotlight, Task Bar, Notification Center, and Teams Popovers.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; controls notes; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Email functionality is limited to eight pre-made templates.
claims.quote: Email functionality is currently limited to the eight provided pre-made templates.
claims.fix: After the template breakdown in What's changing, add: "Microsoft's June 2, 2026 Copilot release notes instead describe nine initial email templates, including a third welcome template, Welcome to Copilot Trial; the organizational messages guide lists eight." The conflicting source is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes#june-2,-2026.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The email templates are not customizable.
claims.quote: The email templates aren't customizable.

claims.claim: The organizational messages guide lists two welcome templates, Welcome to Copilot and Welcome to Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Two welcome messages for Welcome to Copilot and Welcome to Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Six email templates come from the Great Microsoft Copilot Journey and address Copilot onboarding and adoption.
claims.quote: Six templates from the Great Microsoft Copilot Journey that highlight features and best practices to help drive Copilot onboarding and adoption.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pre-made messages do not require approval before delivery.
claims.quote: Selecting a pre-made message doesn't require any approval before the message can be delivered to end users.

claims.claim: The custom-message approval workflow is not an approval gate for the pre-made-only email channel.
claims.quote: Email functionality is currently limited to the eight provided pre-made templates. / Selecting a pre-made message doesn't require any approval before the message can be delivered to end users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft is removing email open tracking worldwide and new open count metrics will no longer be available.
claims.quote: Email open tracking is being removed for Organizational Messages emails worldwide. New open count metrics will no longer be available, but previously collected open count data will remain accessible.

claims.claim: Previously collected email open count data remains accessible.
claims.quote: New open count metrics will no longer be available, but previously collected open count data will remain accessible.

claims.claim: Government environments such as GCC and GCC-H are not supported.
claims.quote: No, government environments such as GCC or GCC-H aren't supported at this time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented Windows tenant policies and Intune configuration are not required for sending organizational messages to email.
claims.quote: Set tenant policies only if you need to deliver messages to Windows surfaces such as Windows Spotlight, Windows Notification Center, and Windows Taskbar. You don't need to set tenant policies for sending messages to Teams Teaching notifications or to Email.

claims.where: summary; controls notes; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationales
claims.claim: Organizational-message authoring requires the Organizational Messages Writer Microsoft Entra role.
claims.quote: To access the organizational messages experiences, you need the Organizational Messages Writer Microsoft Entra role.

claims.claim: The Organizational Messages Approver role is used to review and approve custom messages.
claims.quote: Approvers - Assign the Organizational Messages Approver admin role in the Microsoft 365 admin center to anyone in your organization who is a designated responsible party for approving customized messages.

claims.claim: Authors configure the start date, end date and frequency at the Schedule step.
claims.quote: Schedule: Configure the start date, end date, and frequency when the message is sent to users.

claims.claim: Urgent delivery is not available for email because its only supported locations are Windows 11 Taskbar and Notifications area.
claims.quote: The only locations available are Windows 11 Taskbar and Notifications area.

claims.claim: An administrator can cancel a message before or during delivery.
claims.quote: Canceled - An admin stopped and canceled the message. The cancellation could be either prior or during the delivery of the message.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The organizational messages documentation does not state the sender address used for email.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "sender". Opened the organizational messages guide and FAQ and read the email release-notes excerpts; none specifies a sender address. Sender-authentication results concern Azure Communication Services or Dynamics, not this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The organizational messages documentation does not describe recipient email opt-out.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "opt out" "targeting". Opened the organizational messages guide and FAQ; no email unsubscribe or recipient opt-out is described. Returned opt-out documentation covers Azure Communication Services or Adoption Score, not this email channel.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Advanced features consist of fully customized message creation and targeting by Department, Location, Company and Usage.
claims.quote:
The currently available advanced features for organizational messages are:

- Fully customized message creation.
- Advanced targeting by group level aggregates, including Department, Location, Company, and Usage.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to advanced features requires the tenant to have at least one Microsoft 365 E3 or E5, Office 365 E3 or E5, or Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license.
claims.quote:
Admins and users can access these advanced features for organizational messages when the tenant has at least one of the following licenses:

- Microsoft 365 E3, or E5 license.
- Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5 license.
- Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.claim: The FAQ states that authoring experiences are automatically disabled if license requirements are not met.
claims.quote: The authoring experiences are automatically disabled if license requirements aren't met.

claims.claim: The FAQ says pre-made messages might still be available without the listed licenses.
claims.quote: Pre-made messages might still be available without these licenses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no email-specific price or meter, leaving admin and communications time as the only evidenced cost.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "license" "price"; organizational messages Microsoft 365 email templates licensing schedule. Opened the feature guide and FAQ licensing sections and read email release notes; no organizational-message email price or usage meter was found.

claims.claim: Recipients do not need a Microsoft Entra role to receive organizational messages.
claims.quote: However, end users aren't required to have any Microsoft Entra roles to receive organizational messages.

claims.claim: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products for which the messages are configured.
claims.quote: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products the messages are configured for delivery.

claims.claim: The documented Windows version, Entra-joined device and firewall requirements are specific to Windows delivery.
claims.quote:
Devices - (For Windows) Only Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices are supported.
- Firewall - (For Windows) To ensure users can communicate with organizational messages, open the following endpoints:

claims.claim: Available targeting options depend on the selected message location.
claims.quote: The available targeting options depend on the message location you select.

claims.claim: The documentation does not specify which recipient targeting options are available for email.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "email" "targeting options". Opened the feature guide's Recipients and advanced-targeting sections and the FAQ; read email release-notes excerpts. Windows and Teams options are specified, but no email targeting matrix is given.

claims.claim: The FAQ describes Allow Microsoft messages to display as a control for Windows surfaces, not as a documented email switch.
claims.quote: In the Settings pane, deselect the option Allow Microsoft messages to display. / These steps ensure the Organizational messages platform sends only your organization's messages to Windows surfaces.

claims.claim: Active is a message status indicating current delivery.
claims.quote: Active - Message is currently being delivered to your users.

claims.claim: Completed is a message status indicating successful delivery as defined by start and end dates.
claims.quote: Completed - The message successfully was delivered as defined by start and end dates.

claims.claim: Failed is a documented message status.
claims.quote: Failed - The organizational messages service wasn't able to properly register the message.

claims.claim: Canceled is a documented message status.
claims.quote: Canceled - An admin stopped and canceled the message.
